mechanism_narrative: A continued rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT raises weekday foot traffic and incidental shopping, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks as more trips are chained through commercial areas.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the last 4 weeks after four more weeks of higher WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, or retail mobility falls despite both series continuing to improve.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline and continues edging down, time spent at home is being replaced by out-of-home discretionary activity, which lifts RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 2% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Retail mobility does not increase within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL drops below 2% for two straight weeks, or retail mobility weakens further while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A further rise in GROCERY_PHARM alongside PARKS indicates more routine local trips and higher neighborhood activity, which spills over into nearby retail visits and raises RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve within two weeks of simultaneous increases in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS, or retail mobility declines while both proxies remain elevated.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains deeply suppressed, access friction and fewer downtown trips will keep retail visits below the recent average over the next four weeks; the effect is strongest when WORKPLACES is also weak.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -20% for at least two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while TRANSIT stays below -20% for two weeks, especially if WORKPLACES is not improving.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PARKS signals favorable weather and seasonal outdoor movement, which diverts spending toward non-retail outings and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite PARKS staying above its recent level, or parks activity falls while retail still weakens.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM crosses into sustained positive territory while RESIDENTIAL continues to ease, households are normalizing errand routines and substituting away from home, which lifts RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM turns positive and stays above 0% for two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM turns positive, or retail mobility weakens even as RESIDENTIAL declines.

mechanism_narrative: The recent improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT should continue to feed retail demand with a lag as commuting density rebuilds; the mechanism is active only if both series keep rising from their current depressed levels.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 5 points week-on-week and TRANSIT rises by at least 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT post strong weekly gains.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stops rising and WORKPLACES remains far below baseline, any mobility recovery is commuting-driven rather than leisure-driven, so retail will stay below its recent mean over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL is flat or falling for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES stays below -15%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week average within 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL stops increasing and WORKPLACES remains below -15%.
